articles.headline: OFAC Targets Iran's Global Shadow Banking Networks in Sweeping Action
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned over two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast.' This action aims to disrupt Iran's global shadow banking networks, which are reportedly used to move billions of dollars through the international financial system and provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions.

The designations were issued under Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, targeting certain sectors of the Iranian economy, including its financial sector; E.O. 13224, as amended, a counter-terrorism designation authority; and E.O. 13871, which targets persons operating in various sectors of Iran's metals industry.

Among the sanctioned entities are individuals linked to Mellat Exchange Company and Mina Fashki and Partners Exchange Company, both designated for operating in Iran's financial sector. The action also included several companies based in the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, and Hong Kong, accused of facilitating thousands of financial transactions for Iranian exchange houses.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran Designations and Cuba Sanctions FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran designations and issued Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) related to Cuba sanctions. The Iran designations are part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting individuals involved in facilitating Iranian oil sales and recovering oil proceeds held in third countries.

Specifically, Mohammad Javad Bavand and Majid Taj were designated under E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy. They are described as part of a network of regime insiders tasked with selling Iranian oil and recovering oil proceeds.

In addition, OFAC issued FAQs 1277 and 1278, clarifying its sanctions authority covering Cuba's manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine sectors. The guidance confirms that authorized activities involving Cuba's marine sector, including payments to Cuban ports for authorized trade and certain humanitarian transactions, may continue.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Counter Narcotics and Cyber Designations, Amends Russia-Related GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations related to counter narcotics and cyber activities. Concurrently, OFAC issued an Illicit Drugs General License and an amended Russia-related General License, along with updated Frequently Asked Questions.

The Russia-related General License 131L authorizes certain transactions related to negotiating and entering into contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH, including related maintenance activities. OFAC also amended associated Russia-related FAQs 1224 and 1225.

Separately, the Federal Register published OFAC's document 2026-23908, adding 14 individuals and six entities tied to international narcotics trafficking following determinations signed on November 19, 2026. This action imposes blocking sanctions under Executive Order 14059 against transnational criminal networks, specifically designating the Italian 'Ndrangheta and the Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Hizballah Charity and Smuggling Network
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated Lebanon-based Wa Ta'awanu Association and its founder, Afif Abdel Rida Chouman, for supporting Hizballah under the guise of humanitarian assistance. This action, taken under counterterrorism authority Executive Order 13224, targets Hizballah's use of charitable organizations and illicit financial networks to raise and move funds.

Additionally, OFAC designated members of a Lebanon- and Türkiye-based gold and cash smuggling network tied to Hizballah and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF). These designations aim to disrupt the financial channels used by these groups to fund their activities.
The action underscores the U.S. commitment to combating terrorism financing and preventing terrorist organizations from exploiting legitimate charitable and financial systems.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations Linked to Mexican Cartels
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new counter narcotics and counter terrorism designations, targeting two Guatemalan drug trafficking organizations: Los Lorenzanas and Los Mendoza Drug Trafficking Organization. These groups have been added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.

Los Lorenzanas is identified as a Transnational Terrorist Group and Criminal Organization, while Los Mendoza Drug Trafficking Organization is linked to the Sinaloa Cartel. These designations expose the groups to asset freezes and prohibit U.S. persons from dealing with them.

OFAC also updated the listing of Los Huistas Drug Trafficking Organization to include secondary sanctions risk and links to both the Sinaloa Cartel and Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion. These actions carry secondary sanctions risk under Executive Order 13224, as amended by Executive Order 13886.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran Designation Update
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) released an update to its Iran designations. This action is part of ongoing efforts to address Iran's illicit activities and financial networks.

While specific details of the update were not immediately provided in the initial announcement, such updates typically involve additions or modifications to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List or other sanctions lists, targeting individuals or entities involved in proliferation, terrorism, or human rights abuses.
These updates reinforce the U.S. government's commitment to maintaining pressure on the Iranian regime to curb its destabilizing behavior.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations. These actions are part of the U.S. government's strategy to counter the Iranian regime's destabilizing activities and its support for terrorism.
The designations aim to further disrupt networks that provide financial, material, technological, or other support to individuals and entities already subject to U.S. sanctions.
Such measures typically involve freezing assets of designated individuals and entities and prohibiting U.S. persons from engaging in transactions with them.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations; Cuba Sanctions Expanded
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations designations, alongside new Cuba designations and the publication of a Cuba-related determination. The U.S. issued a determination paving the way for sanctions on the electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors of the Cuban economy.

The determination was issued as the U.S. imposed fresh Cuba-related sanctions on people and entities, targeting a crude oil shipping network, state-owned entities, and China-based suppliers of Cuba's military forces.

The State Department designated eight entities and two individuals and identified five vessels as blocked property under Executive Order 14404. The sanctioned Chinese companies, China National Electronic Import and Export Company (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation, were accused of supplying equipment to Cuba's military.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Updates Listings, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, updates to certain Iran-related listings, and the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert. Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and Frequently Asked Question.
The Iran-related OFAC Alert focuses on 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion,' highlighting deceptive practices used to circumvent sanctions.

The amended Venezuela-related General License and FAQ likely provide updated guidance on permissible transactions involving Venezuela, as U.S. sanctions on Venezuela remain in force but have been eased through licenses since January 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Iran General License FF-1, titled 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.'

This general license provides a limited authorization for affected parties to terminate dealings with the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, which is subject to Iran-related sanctions.
Such wind-down licenses are common when an entity is designated, allowing for an orderly cessation of business to minimize unintended economic disruptions.

articles.headline: EU Imposes Stricter Export Restrictions on 15 Russian Entities, Removes One Chinese Firm
body: The Council of the European Union has decided to add 15 Russian entities to the list of those subject to stricter export restrictions on dual-use goods and advanced technologies. These entities are reportedly part of Russia's military-industrial complex or have links to its defense and security sector.

This action aims to further increase pressure on Russia to end its war of aggression in Ukraine. The decision directly impacts European universities, research institutions, and technology transfer offices by broadening mandatory end-user screening and technical data transfer controls.

Concurrently, the Council also decided to remove one entity from the list, lifting export restrictions imposed on it. This Chinese firm reportedly ceased the activities that led to its inclusion and provided credible assurances against trading sensitive goods with Russia.

articles.headline: EU Proposes 22nd Sanctions Package Against Russia, Targeting Banks, Crypto, and Sports
body: The European Commission has proposed its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, targeting its banks, crypto platforms, and participation in sporting events. Key elements include extending transaction bans to approximately 60 additional Russian banks, removing them from the SWIFT system.

The package also introduces a dedicated Crypto Sanctions Task Force to combat third-country cryptocurrency networks used for evasion, and expands the energy services ban to prevent European companies from assisting Russia's energy infrastructure.

Furthermore, the proposals include a ban on Russian teams and individual athletes competing under the country's flag at events in the European Union, restrictions on financial flows from Russian sponsors to EU-based sports and cultural associations, and a visa ban for Russian ex-combatants.

articles.headline: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
body: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

body: All three main US indexes were down in early trading, with the tech-dominated Nasdaq down almost 4%.

articles.headline: My family were killed in Ukraine. My mum blamed Zelensky's troops - the truth is complicated
body: BBC journalist Anastasiya Gribanova investigates who killed her father and grandparents in the war.

articles.headline: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
body: Despite widespread concern from residents ahead of the blast, officials say that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.

articles.headline: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
body: Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, was killed with his wife and two teenage daughters, doctors say.

articles.headline: Protesters call on Israel to free Palestinian student held without charge
body: Mahdi Tunsi, 26, was taken from his university dormitory earlier this month and has since been held without charge.

articles.headline: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 76 held hostage for 17 hours
body: One gunman was killed after what the country's president described as a robbery of a cash-laden armoured car gone wrong.

articles.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
body: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.

articles.headline: Canadian astronaut welcomes baby girl from space station
body: Joshua Kutryk, currently on his first space mission, is just the fourth astronaut in history to miss the birth of a child while aboard the International Space Station.

articles.headline: Thomas Markle charged in US for possessing child sex abuse images
body: The FBI arrested Markle on 6 November after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles uncovered the abuse material.

articles.headline: Two children among six dead after plane crash off Mississippi coast
body: Divers found the bodies of three adult, one teenager aged 16, and two boys, aged 12 and 10, in the wreckage.

articles.headline: Veteran Nigerian Nollywood actor Pete Edochie dies aged 79
body: Odochie rose to prominence in 1987 after starring in a television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's acclaimed novel Things Fall Apart.

articles.headline: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court battle over impeachment threat
body: The break-in happened in 2020, when thieves allegedly stole bundles of US dollar bills hidden inside a sofa at the farm.

articles.headline: Moment Chinese space mission lifts off with first Pakistan astronaut aboard
body: China launched its Shenzhou-24 space mission to bring three astronauts to its Tiangong space station.

articles.headline: Watch: Flock of turkeys chases woman on Massachusetts pavement
body: The woman said she had to jump into a stranger's car to escape a flock of turkeys that chased her down the sidewalk.

articles.headline: Watch: Moment troops raid home and capture Mexican drug lord
body: Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops detained 'El Chapo Isidro', who had managed to evade capture for years.

articles.headline: Cheers and applause as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia office
body: BBC's Lily Jamali reports from Nvidia's headquarters, where she gauges the reaction to Huang's return after Trump says he brokered a deal.

articles.headline: First Lady Melania Trump welcomes this year's White House Christmas tree
body: The official 2026 White House Christmas tree is an 18-foot fir from Silent Night Evergreens, a farm in Endeavor, Wisconsin.
